note_2026_08_13_slip_in_chat:
Session driven entirely by the shop asking, over and over in different words, 'why isn't the order confirmation a card?' — and being RIGHT, while I spent two turns answering the wrong half of the question. Two commits: d66df0a (the feature) and the fdc3f9e debug removal.

  (1) THE CONFUSION TO NEVER REPEAT, because it has now burned parts of three sessions. There are THREE distinct LINE messages around a new order and they look interchangeable in a screenshot:
    (a) buildOrderFlex pushed to the CUSTOMER via pushToUser — a real Flex card, has worked continuously since it was written, never broken;
    (b) sendOrderToLine's `https://line.me/R/oaMessage/...` deep link — the message the CUSTOMER sends, prefilled, tapping Send themselves. LINE's oaMessage scheme carries PLAIN TEXT ONLY. This one genuinely cannot ever be a card, in any codebase, for any merchant — it is not a limitation of this app;
    (c) pushNewOrderNotification to STAFF — existed, but sent plain text, and had NEVER fired even once because LINE_ORDER_NOTIFY_TO was empty.
  The shop's 'ตอนแรกยังได้เลย' (it worked at first!) was accurate and I nearly argued with it: they had been testing AS THE CUSTOMER, so they saw (a) land in their own chat. Later they were looking at the OA inbox — the STAFF side — where only (b) arrives. Nothing regressed; (a) and (b) are simply different messages to different people. When a screenshot shows a plain-text order, FIRST establish whether the bubble is incoming or outgoing and whose phone it is.

  (2) THE ACTUAL BUG NOBODY HAD NAMED, found by reading pages/api/verify-slip.js rather than by theorising: the order-confirmation message tells customers 'กรุณาแนบสลิปการโอนในแชทนี้' — attach your slip in this chat — and they do exactly that. But slip verification only ever ran from the WEBSITE's upload field, so an image sent into the LINE chat reached nothing. The order stayed 'pending' forever, buildPaymentConfirmedFlex never fired, and a human had to type a holding reply by hand. The app's own copy was steering customers into a dead end. Measured at the time: 68 orders across 5 customers stuck in 'pending', one account alone holding 53.

  (3) BUILT: slips sent as an image into the 1:1 OA chat are now accepted. pages/api/line-webhook.js grew an image-message branch that pulls the file from LINE's separate media host (api-data.line.me/v2/bot/message/{id}/content, 10MB cap), finds that customer's newest 'pending' order by line_user_id, and runs it through the SAME path as the website. New lib/slipVerification.js owns storage + SlipOK + mark-paid so both doors leave the order in identical state; it deliberately sends no LINE message itself, because the two callers differ (the web route pushes, the webhook replies with the replyToken it was handed). Answers with buildPaymentConfirmedFlex when the bank confirms, else a NEW buildSlipReceivedFlex ('ได้รับสลิปแล้ว', same visual family, carries result.error as the reason) so the chat never dead-ends on silence.
    - SAFETY PROPERTIES, all deliberate: images in the staff GROUP are ignored outright (a group photo must never touch an order); a customer with NO pending order gets no reply at all, so an ordinary photo is silently left to human staff; and a wrong-amount slip FAILS CLOSED — SlipOK's amount check refuses to mark anything paid and the customer is told the amount doesn't match. Worst case is a false negative, never a wrongly-paid order.
    - KNOWN LIMITATION, accepted: matching is 'newest pending order for this lineUserId'. With stale pending orders lying around (see 2) a slip can be matched against the wrong one, but the amount check then rejects it rather than mis-crediting.

  (4) STAFF ALERT CONVERTED TO A CARD. pushNewOrderNotification (hand-built plain text) replaced by pushOrderCardToStaff(flexMessage); pages/api/orders.js now builds buildOrderFlex ONCE and sends the identical card to both the customer and LINE_ORDER_NOTIFY_TO.

  (5) THE userId WAS IN THE DATABASE THE WHOLE TIME. The previous session left fdc3f9e — a `?showUserId=1` window.alert() — live on production purely to read the shop's own LINE userId off their phone, and it sat there for a day. It was never needed: `SELECT line_user_id, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1` immediately surfaced U9ac6027ce4ed4ec187a6616cf14184a2 with 61 orders, latest one placed at the exact minute shown in the shop's screenshot. Confirmed with the shop before using it (an unconfirmed guess here would have pointed every order alert at a real customer's phone — a genuine privacy failure), then set in Vercel Production and the debug code removed. LESSON: before shipping debug code to production to read a value off someone's device, check whether the app already stores it.

  (6) PRODUCTION ROLLBACK INCIDENT — my error, ~6-8 minutes of old code live. `vercel ls lovepier --prod | tail -12` hides the header and the NEWEST rows, so the first URL in that truncated view was 19h old; `vercel redeploy` on it rebuilt that ancient commit over the current one. Caught within minutes because /api/line-webhook started returning 404 while /api/orders still answered 400 — i.e. some routes existed and one didn't, which only a version mismatch explains. Fixed by redeploying the genuinely newest deployment and re-probing every route. TAKEAWAY: `vercel ls --prod` is newest-first WITH a header; never pipe it through `tail`, and always confirm a deployment's age before redeploying it.

  (7) HOW THIS WAS VERIFIED WITHOUT PLACING REAL ORDERS, reusable: every webhook path returns 200 by design, so the HTTP status proves nothing. Response TIME was used as the signal instead — an image event from a user runs a DB lookup (~1-3s on prod, ~900ms local) while an ignored one returns in ~2ms locally / ~0.4s on prod. Comparing the two against each other, on the same deploy, distinguishes 'the new branch ran' from 'the route ignored it', and was also what proved the rollback in (6). Order-matching itself was checked with a read-only SQL query mirroring the webhook's own WHERE clause. NOT VERIFIED: the actual LINE image download and a real SlipOK call — both need real credentials and a real slip, and placing a real order is forbidden per the standing gotcha.

  (8) A SUSPECTED BUG THAT TURNED OUT NOT TO EXIST, recorded so it isn't 'fixed' again: verify-slip's storeSlip passed a Node Buffer to Supabase Storage, which is exactly the pattern that corrupted every admin image upload before 40029ca. I assumed slips in production were therefore corrupt — then actually fetched three of them and checked the magic bytes: all valid JPEGs (ffd8ffe0). The corruption never affected this path. The code was still moved to the Blob form for consistency, and the comment there says plainly that it is NOT a bug fix.

  (9) STILL OPEN AT END OF SESSION: no real end-to-end test had been run yet — the shop was asked to place one order and send a slip in the chat, and had not reported back. Also unresolved: the 68 stuck 'pending' orders are not retroactively fixed by any of this (a customer re-sending an old slip now would be matched against their NEWEST order, and rejected on amount), so they need clearing by hand in /admin. And now that the staff card works, sendOrderToLine's plain-text message (b in (1)) is arguably redundant noise that also forces the customer to tap Send — offered to remove it, no answer yet.

Symptom: a placed order never posted a message into the LINE OA's own chat inbox (what staff actually watch), even though the customer's OWN order-confirmation card (server pushToUser, via LINE_MESSAGING_TOKEN) kept arriving the entire time — that one fact ruled out a broken/revoked channel token immediately and kept the investigation scoped correctly. The mechanism that's supposed to make an order show up as a new incoming-looking chat message is `liff.sendMessages()` in lib/liff.js (posts the order card INTO the chat as if the customer sent it themselves) — LINE-documented as working ONLY inside LINE's own in-app browser, and needing (a) `chat_message.write` scope on the LIFF channel, (b) that channel's 'Linked LINE Official Account' actually set, (c) a normal personal LINE account (not the OA's own Business ID) that's really a friend of the OA, (d) a current LINE app version. Walked the shop through checking every one of these live, over many screenshots of LINE Developers Console / LINE Official Account Manager / the App Store:
    - chat_message.write — was ALREADY enabled. Not the cause.
    - Linked OA — was blank ('-'). THIS WAS a real, separate bug and the shop fixed it themselves (pointed it at the real OA, @694eccdr/Lovepier.Cafe). Correct fix, but did not alone resolve the symptom.
    - First re-test was invalid: the shop tested logged in as the OA's own Business ID, which is not equivalent to a customer (not a 'friend' of its own OA in the normal sense) — redone with a real personal account, still failed.
    - LINE app version — confirmed already latest (App Store showed 'เปิด', not 'อัปเดต'). Ruled out.
    - A Webhook 401 (SlipOK's own endpoint, https://api.slipok.com/api/line/webhook/71639) surfaced by the shop mid-investigation via the console's own 'Verify' button — explained as UNRELATED and NOT chased further: webhooks carry INCOMING events to a server, sendMessages() is an outgoing client call that never touches the channel's webhook at all; a message it successfully posts would show in the OA inbox regardless of any webhook's HTTP status. Worth the shop fixing separately for SlipOK's own auto-scan feature, but it is not this bug.
    - The actual error, finally: extracted with a TEMPORARY window.alert() debug build (012fecb, reverted immediately after in c6921ef — deployed, had the shop test a real order on their phone, read the popup, reverted within ~10 minutes) — `Unexpected API name`, a LINE-app-NATIVE bridge error, not a JS/config error, occurring even with every item above confirmed correct.     - PIVOTED to the robust alternative instead of continuing to chase sendMessages(): `LINE_ORDER_NOTIFY_TO` (lib/lineMessaging.js's pushNewOrderNotification — already existed, was always the intended fallback for exactly this kind of fragility) pushes a plain-text alert directly from the server via LINE_MESSAGING_TOKEN to a specific userId/groupId, independent of how/where the customer opened the page.

note_2026_08_12_line_oa_group_alert:
Tail end of the same 2026-08-12 run. Shop asked again 'ทำไมถึงไม่แจ้งเตือนในไลน์oa' and then 'ทำให้แจ้งเตือนกลับไปในกลุ่มไลน์oa ด้วย ตอนนี้กลับมาเป็นแบบเดิมอีกแล้ว...ตอนแรกก็สามารถส่งการแจ้งเตือนในไลน์ได้แล้ว', with a screenshot of the OA chat showing an order card (LP260812-6276) that HAD arrived.

  (1) THE SCREENSHOT IS A RED HERRING, and this is the thing to get straight before touching anything. There are TWO independent notification paths and they keep getting conflated: pushToUser() sends the Flex order card to the CUSTOMER's own chat (working the entire time, and it's what that screenshot shows — the shop was testing with their own phone as the customer, name 'แก้ว'), while pushNewOrderNotification() is the plain-text alert meant for STAFF. Long single session, all in one push (de74fcf) because the shop kept adding requests mid-flow rather than stopping to verify each one live — see syncStatus for why production is unverified. Seven pieces of work, roughly in the order asked.

  (0) HOW TO SCREENSHOT THE LOCAL DEV SITE FOR THE SHOP — new technique this session, worth reusing. The in-app Browser pane's `computer` click tool is unreliable here (clicks silently landing as text-selection or missing the target after a layout shift — same tab, same page, no visible cause found). But to actually SEND real image files to the shop (not just view them myself), Playwright driving the Mac's own installed Chrome does the job and the Browser pane cannot: `npx --yes playwright screenshot -b chromium --channel chrome --viewport-size "402,784" --user-agent "<iPhone Safari UA>" --wait-for-timeout 1200 <url> <file>.png` (channel=chrome reuses /Applications/Google Chrome.app, so no ~150MB browser download). For a multi-step walkthrough (not just one screenshot), `npm install --no-save playwright` into the scratchpad dir and drive it with a small .mjs script using `chromium.launch({channel:'chrome'})` + `page.click(..., {force:true})` — force is required because the Next.js dev-mode `<nextjs-portal>` (the floating N badge) intercepts pointer events and blocks normal Playwright clicks even when the target is visibly clear. SendUserFile then delivers the PNGs to the shop's actual phone.

  (1) BACK ARROW MADE PROMINENT (first fix, small). StepHeader's ‹ was `text-black/40 text-lg` — same faint weight as the ✕ close button despite being the one control used on every screen. Session fixed the whole event-image + event-save path, then removed the /events spotlight and ran an `impeccable polish` pass on the home page. Six commits, all pushed.

  (1) HEIC UPLOAD (cbb4d6b). Shop could not upload iPhone photos to events: the image just never appeared. Two stacked causes. First, `app/api/admin/upload/route.ts` resizes with sharp, and the sharp build here has NO HEVC decoder (`sharp.format.heif.input.fileSuffix` is only ['.avif']; encoding hevc fails with 'heifsave: Unsupported compression'), so .heic 500s. Second, EventModal.handleUpload had NO catch, so the 500 was swallowed silently — it looked like 'upload finished, image missing'. Fix: `lib/upload-image.ts` now detects HEIC (mime image/heic|heif OR .heic/.heif extension — HEIC often reports an empty MIME) and converts to JPEG in the browser via heic2any before POSTing; all callers (events, promotions, menu) share this lib. EventModal got try/catch + toast on both the main image and the album loop, plus accept=".heic,.heif".

  (2) BINARY CORRUPTION ON VERCEL (40029ca) — the important one. After the HEIC fix images uploaded but rendered BROKEN, returning HTTP 200. Forensics: fetched bytes started `52494646 efbfbd...` (RIFF then U+FFFD) and the file was LARGER than a real webp. Root cause: supabase-js sends a Node `Buffer` as a raw fetch body, and the Vercel serverless runtime coerces that body to a UTF-8 string, so every byte >= 0x80 becomes EF BF BD. LOCALHOST DOES NOT REPRODUCE IT (undici handles the Buffer as binary) — a clean local test proves nothing here. Fix: pass `new Blob([new Uint8Array(webp)], {type:'image/webp'})` so supabase-js sends binary-safe multipart. The Uint8Array wrap is required because @types/node v26 rejects Buffer as a BlobPart. Applied to app/api/admin/upload/route.ts and lib/menuImport/imageProcess.ts. lib/upload-promotion-image.ts is client-side and already passed a Blob. >>> ANY IMAGE UPLOADED BEFORE 40029ca IS PERMANENTLY CORRUPT AND MUST BE RE-UPLOADED.

  (3) BLANK EVENT DATE (f99171d). Saving an event failed with a bare 'เกิดข้อผิดพลาด'. A blank date field posts '', and both routes did `body.eventDate ?? null` — '' is not nullish, so '' reached the `date` column and Postgres threw 'Invalid time value'. Changed to `|| null` in POST and PUT, wrapped insert/update in try/catch that returns the real DB message, and surfaced it in the admin toast so a failed save is no longer opaque.

  (a) IMAGE FOLDER STRUCTURE — the answer is that it does not matter. classifyImages() in lib/menuImport/imageMatch.ts strips folder names and matches on BASENAME only, and imageClient.ts accepts all three input shapes (a .zip expanded in-browser with fflate, a webkitdirectory folder pick, or a drag-drop that walks entries). So per-category subfolders are fine. The real constraints told to the shop: filenames must be UNIQUE ACROSS ALL FOLDERS (since folders are ignored, the same basename in two categories is a conflict), must equal image_code (or image_file when set), must be .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp (HEIC is rejected at match time, not converted — that is a different path from the event uploader), and must not end in ' (1)'. Recommended the FOLDER picker over .zip: expandZip does arrayBuffer()+unzipSync, i.e. the whole archive in browser memory at once, which will not survive a few hundred phone-sized originals.

  (b) WHY NOTHING SHOWED — three independent gates, all found by reading rather than guessing: categories.is_active=true in lib/db/menuPageData.js (the 10 import categories were seeded false), menu_items.is_available=true (the 21 incomplete rows are forced false), and TAB_SECTION_CATS in components/menu/menuData.js only knew the 7 hand-built categories, so even an active import category had no tab and was unreachable.

Enabling all 10 without touching the old ones would have shown customers two parallel menus. Shop chose REPLACE. Result: 212 items visible (233 minus the 21 incomplete), 60 legacy items hidden.

TAB_SECTION_CATS now defines 10 tabs and each one lists its import category FIRST and the legacy equivalent AFTER, so reactivating an old category later lands it in the right tab instead of creating a duplicate tab. SECTION_IDS and the tab labels are derived from that one map (TAB_LABELS replaced three hand-maintained per-language arrays). MenuExperience.js renders sections from the map in a single loop, replacing SEVEN near-identical hardcoded blocks, and hides any tab whose categories are inactive or have no items (previously such a tab was a dead scroll target, because scrollTo() silently no-ops on a missing anchor). getSrcSet learned the import path menu/<code>/960.webp — it only understood the legacy '-960w.webp' suffix — and imageVersion now flows through menuPageData.js -> buildMenuData -> withImageVersion() as a ?v= cache-buster, which matters because re-uploading an image reuses the same storage path. menuAddOnsForCategory also now answers for 'coffee-drinks' (that is why the drinks section renders 59 rows for 57 DB items: the 2 espresso add-ons).

A percentage `height` (even `height:100%`) resolves against the parent's `height` property, NOT its used height. A parent sized by flex or by `min-height` has `height:auto`, so the child computes to 0 and silently disappears. Stretch it with flex instead, or size it in vh.

Size anything in the LINE in-app browser against viewport HEIGHT, not width. LINE's own chrome eats ~45px, so a layout that just fits at 402x784 in a normal browser is below the fold there; a vw-based clamp gives a tall phone the same cramped band as a short one.

--nav-h is published by whichever chrome is sticky at the top: the site Nav on normal pages, OrderFlow's StepHeader on /delivery (Layout unmounts the Nav there). Anything new that sticks below it must offset by --nav-h, and any new top chrome must publish it and clear it on unmount.

Reading scrollTop/getBoundingClientRect right after setting a scroll returns the PRE-scroll value, because scroll-behavior is smooth — this reads as 'the pane cannot scroll' and it is wrong. ~/.npm has root-owned files — install with `--cache <writable dir>`.

OrderFlow's wizard steps swap in place (no real page navigation), so nothing resets scroll on step change by itself. Any content newly added near the top of a step can render already scrolled past if the previous step was tall enough to scroll. Fixed generally with `useEffect(() => window.scrollTo(0,0), [step])` — keep this if the step machinery is ever refactored.

customers.phone, not customers.line_user_id, is the right upsert key for '/api/orders' — LINE login can fail or be silently skipped (this is even easier to trigger locally, since the LIFF-disabled test trick used to reach steps 2+ never populates lineUserId at all), but phone is always required to place an order. A partial unique index (`WHERE phone <> ''`) is needed since phone defaults to ''.

To send the shop an actual screenshot file (not just view one myself), the in-app Browser pane's `computer` click tool is unreliable on this app (silent no-ops/mis-clicks with no clear cause) and SendUserFile needs a real file on disk anyway. `npx playwright screenshot -b chromium --channel chrome --viewport-size "402,784" --user-agent "<iPhone UA>" <url> <file>.png` reuses the Mac's installed Chrome (no ~150MB download) and produces a real PNG. For a multi-step walkthrough, `npm install --no-save playwright` into the scratchpad and drive it with a small script — but pass `{force:true}` to every `.click()`, because the Next.js dev-mode `<nextjs-portal>` badge intercepts pointer events and blocks normal Playwright clicks even on a clearly visible target.

liff.sendMessages() can throw a native 'Unexpected API name' bridge error even when chat_message.write scope, the LINE Login channel's Linked OA, and the LINE app version are all confirmed correct — suspected cause is that it needs an actual in-room/chat launch context, which a Rich-Menu-triggered LIFF launch may not satisfy even though isApiAvailable('sendMessages') itself reports true. Don't sink more time chasing this path; LINE_ORDER_NOTIFY_TO (server-side Messaging API push, lib/lineMessaging.js) is the robust alternative — it doesn't depend on launch context, LIFF, or any client-side quirk at all.

A LINE Login channel's 'Linked LINE Official Account' (Add friend option) can silently be unset ('-') even after the LIFF app's own scope and everything else about it is configured correctly — sendMessages() needs it pointed at the real OA to have anywhere to post the message.

Testing an OA's own features by logging into LINE with the OA's own Business ID account is NOT equivalent to testing as a real customer — it isn't a normal 'friend' of its own OA. Must use an ordinary personal LINE account that's added the OA as a friend the normal way.

A webhook returning a non-200 (e.g. SlipOK's endpoint 401ing on LINE's own 'Verify' check) is unrelated to liff.sendMessages() or any client push — webhooks only carry INCOMING events to a server. Don't conflate the two paths when debugging a 'no notification' report.

LINE Flex message text with no natural word-break can get split MID-WORD by LINE's own auto-wrap, because Thai has no inter-word spaces for the wrap algorithm to use — e.g. 'ออเดอร์' became 'ออเด'/'อร์' across a line. Insert an explicit \n at a sensible point; Flex text honors literal newlines regardless of wrap:true.

A window.alert() gated behind a URL query param (e.g. ?showUserId=1) or a specific failure branch is a fast, safe way to read real client-side state/errors off someone's actual phone in production when there's no remote debugger available — deploy, have them test once, capture the exact string, then revert within minutes. Never leave one live longer than needed, even a gated one (see fdc3f9e in syncStatus if it's still there). AND BEFORE REACHING FOR THIS AT ALL: check whether the app already stores the value you want — fdc3f9e sat live on production for a day to read a userId that was sitting in the orders table the whole time.

`vercel ls <project> --prod` is NEWEST-FIRST and has a header row, so piping it through `tail` shows you the OLDEST rows and hides the newest. Doing that and then running `vercel redeploy` on the first URL you see rolls production BACK — it happened on 2026-08-13 and put a 19h-old build on www.lovepier.cafe for several minutes. Read that listing from the top, and check the Age column before redeploying anything.

LINE's `https://line.me/R/oaMessage/{oaId}/?{text}` deep link (components/delivery/OrderFlow.js sendOrderToLine) can carry PLAIN TEXT ONLY — it opens the customer's own compose box prefilled and they tap Send. It can never be a Flex card, in any app, for any merchant. A card in the OA chat has to come from the SERVER (Messaging API push, needs LINE_ORDER_NOTIFY_TO) or from liff.sendMessages (which is broken here). When someone asks 'why isn't that message a card', first work out WHICH of the three order messages they mean — see note_2026_08_13_slip_in_chat (1).

A payment slip sent as an IMAGE into the LINE OA chat and a slip uploaded on the website are two completely different doors, and only the website one used to be wired up — so an order could sit 'pending' forever while the customer had genuinely paid and been told (by our own copy) to attach it in the chat. Both doors now run lib/slipVerification.js. If slip handling is ever changed, change it there, not in one route.

Every branch of /api/line-webhook returns 200 on purpose (LINE disables a webhook that errors), so an HTTP status proves nothing about which branch ran. Use response TIME instead: a branch that queries the DB takes ~1-3s on production versus ~0.4s for one that returns immediately. Comparing two payloads against each other on the same deploy is what distinguishes 'my new code ran' from 'it was ignored' — and is also how a bad deploy got caught.

CORRECTION to an older gotcha/note (2026-08-13, note_2026_08_12_line_oa_group_alert item 9): a Postgres 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification' error on the customers-table upsert was dismissed there as 'stale log noise, re-confirmed the index exists, not a live bug'. That check only confirmed the partial index EXISTS via pg_indexes — it never tested whether a real `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (phone) DO UPDATE` actually matches it. It doesn't: a partial unique index (`WHERE phone <> ''`) can't be inferred as an ON CONFLICT arbiter unless the same WHERE is repeated in the query (drizzle-orm: pass `targetWhere`). This was a real, silent bug from 2026-08-05/0005's migration until 2026-08-17's a0498d4 — every new phone number failed to get a customers row, non-fatally swallowed by the surrounding try/catch. If a similar-looking error resurfaces in a log dump, reproduce it directly (a real INSERT, not just an index-existence check) before dismissing it as noise again.

A pure-calc module meant to be imported from BOTH a client component and server code (e.g. a price/points preview shown live in the UI, recomputed authoritatively on the server) must contain ZERO imports of DB/Node-only packages, even transitively — importing `./db` (drizzle + `postgres`) from the same file as the calc function breaks the CLIENT bundle only (Turbopack 'Module not found: fs / perf_hooks'), which neither `tsc --noEmit` nor `vitest run` will ever catch since neither builds a browser bundle. Split into a zero-dependency calc file and a separate DB-writing file, and always load the actual page in a browser preview after touching a file like this, not just typecheck/test.

A DrizzleQueryError's `.message` is just "Failed query: <sql>" — the actual Postgres error (code, constraint_name, detail) is nested at `err.cause`, not in the message string. A `String(err.message).includes(...)` check for a specific constraint violation (e.g. to detect-and-ignore a duplicate-insert race) will silently never match; check `err.cause?.code` (Postgres SQLSTATE, e.g. '23505' for unique_violation) and `err.cause?.constraint_name` instead. Caught only by deliberately re-triggering the race in a throwaway script and watching it throw instead of no-op.

To exercise a 'recognized returning LINE customer' code path locally without real LIFF OAuth (which automated browser testing can't complete — it hits a real accounts.line.me/access.line.me redirect that gets blocked), add a temporary useEffect gated behind a distinctive URL query param (e.g. `?__test_profile__=1`) that calls `setProfile({userId, displayName})` directly with a REAL existing customer's lineUserId from the DB — this drives every downstream effect (recognition lookup, cached-distance bypass, etc.) exactly as a real login would, using real data already in the database. A 'use server' module may only export async functions. A plain const or type export there makes Next.js drop the whole module's exports at build time, and the error points at the importing file, not the cause. Shared constants/types for a server-action module go in a normal file (see lib/inStore.ts).
Cormorant Garamond has no baht glyph, so a bare ฿ inside .font-display falls back to a Thai face with mismatched metrics and overlaps the first digit. Wrap it: ฿.

App Router treats a folder whose name starts with _ as private — it produces no route. Cost a 404 while building a scratch preview page.

A bare `db.select().from(orders)` (no column projection) makes drizzle enumerate every column DECLARED IN schema.ts, not every column that exists in the database. So adding a column to schema.ts and deploying before the migration runs breaks every one of those call sites at once — in this repo that is app/admin/actions/orders.ts:16, pages/order/[orderNo].js and pages/api/verify-slip.js, i.e. the whole admin orders page, the customer's own order link, and slip verification for orders that were already paid. Additive schema changes here are NOT safe to deploy ahead of their migration. Apply the SQL first, verify with the script's AFTER probe, then deploy.

Server components and getServerSideProps format dates on VERCEL, where the process timezone is UTC — so any `toLocaleString`/`toLocaleDateString` on a timestamp needs an explicit `timeZone: 'Asia/Bangkok'` or it renders 7 hours early in production and correctly on a shop laptop, which is the worst way for a bug to behave. This was already live for createdAt in app/admin/orders/page.tsx before anyone noticed. Related and still unfixed on purpose: makeOrderNo() in pages/api/orders.js builds its date prefix from the process timezone too.

On the /delivery summary step the LEGACY components/delivery/CartDrawer.js is still mounted alongside OrderFlow's own UI, and it has its own buttons with overlapping text — notably 'ไปชำระเงิน฿NNNN' and 'ดำเนินการต่อ'. Automation that clicks by text match will silently drive the wrong component (this looked exactly like 'the click does nothing'). OrderFlow's real summary CTA is '^ถัดไป฿' and its real menu-step advance is the floating '^ตะกร้า N$' button; the drawer's 'ดำเนินการต่อ' is NOT the wizard. Match anchored patterns, and check `offsetParent !== null` plus the button's index before trusting a text hit.

th-TH's ICU `weekday: 'short'` is 'พฤหัส' — long enough to overflow a half-width <select>. When a Thai date label has to fit a control, use the abbreviation tables in lib/preorder.js (formatDayThai / formatSlotThai, 'พฤ.') rather than toLocaleDateString, which has the side benefit of matching what the LINE Flex card shows.

A settings value whose BLANK is meaningful cannot use this repo's usual `m[KEY] ? num(m[KEY]) : default` idiom — '' is falsy, so the default silently comes back and the shop's change appears not to save. shop_closed_days is the live example ('' means open every day, unset means the Wednesday closure): it reads through parseClosedDays(), which distinguishes null/undefined from '', and its saveSettings() put() deliberately has no `|| '3'` fallback. Check any new setting for this before copying the numeric pattern.

Two-phase membership feature, both shipped and deployed.

PHASE 1 — Love Pier ID (e66bd2b). New LIFF page pages/member.js + pages/api/member.js. A LINE-logged-in customer registers with name, phone and an OPTIONAL birthday (collected for a future birthday promo, never required) and gets a member card showing a member number, a QR code, and their existing points balance.

The two-code design is the part to preserve: customers.member_no is the readable number staff read aloud or type (formatted LP001 by formatMemberNo() in pages/api/member.js — display formatting only, the column stores a bare integer), while customers.member_code is a separate crypto.randomBytes(24).toString('base64url') secret and is what the QR actually encodes, as the payload "LPID1:<code>". Putting the sequential number in the QR would let anyone impersonate a nearby member by typing their number. The LPID1: prefix is a version marker so the payload format can change later without invalidating issued cards.

member_no comes from a Postgres SEQUENCE (customers_member_no_seq), not SELECT MAX+1, and is assigned by an UPDATE ... WHERE member_no IS NULL. That combination makes a repeat or racing POST a safe no-op: it re-issues nothing and burns no sequence value. Registration keys on the verified lineUserId FIRST and only falls back to the upsert-by-phone pattern from pages/api/orders.js when no row exists, so a customer who already ordered delivery keeps their row and their points instead of getting a duplicate.

PHASE 2 — in-store counter flow (36a7f2a). /admin/scan (app/admin/scan/page.tsx + components/admin/scan-terminal.tsx) behind the existing admin session. Staff scan the QR, or type the member number when a screen will not scan — the manual path is always visible, not a fallback that appears after failure. Then they enter the gross bill; the app applies the member discount, records the sale, credits points, and pushes the customer a receipt card in LINE.

Rates are admin settings, NOT constants — in_store_discount_percent and in_store_baht_per_point (defaults 10 and 1, i.e. 700 -> 630 -> 630 points). Deliberately separate keys from the delivery rates: delivery still gives no instant discount and earns 1 point per 20 baht, and neither should move when the other does. recordInStoreVisit re-reads both from settings at confirm time, so a scan tab left open overnight cannot apply a stale rate.

An in-store visit is written as an orders row because the loyalty ledger keys off an order id — point_transactions.order_id UNIQUE is what stops one purchase crediting twice. note_2026_08_20_preorder:
PRE-ORDER (สั่งล่วงหน้า) — built end to end this session, NOT committed, NOT deployed, migration NOT applied.

WHAT THE SHOP ASKED FOR (their four decisions, do not re-litigate): works for BOTH delivery and pickup; payment stays immediate at order time (the existing PromptPay + SlipOK path is untouched, no pay-later); the customer picks an HOURLY SLOT derived from shop hours, not a free time input; and the scheduled time shows on the EXISTING /admin/orders cards with upcoming pre-orders sorted to the top — no new admin page.

THE DESIGN, and why:

(a) ONE COLUMN, orders.scheduled_for timestamptz, nullable. NULL = ASAP, which is what every pre-existing order already was, so no backfill. Chosen over a date + 'HH:MM' text pair because Thailand is a fixed UTC+7 with no DST, so the wall-clock<->instant conversion is exact and reversible with a literal '+07:00'; because two columns make a half-set schedule representable; and because one timestamptz compares against now() and sorts against created_at with no casting.

(b) lib/preorder.js IS THE WHOLE FEATURE'S BRAIN and IMPORTS NOTHING — not ./db, not ./settings, not a date library. Both the client picker and pages/api/orders.js call the same functions, so the server can never disagree with what the customer was shown. Exports: parseClosedDays, weekdayOfYmd, bangkokDateParts, bangkokSlotToInstant, addDaysYmd, slotsForDate, availableDates, formatSlotThai, formatDayThai, validateScheduleRequest. Every function takes `now` as an injectable option, which is what makes all 36 unit tests deterministic. No Intl anywhere in it: conversion is a fixed +420-minute shift read back through the getUTC* accessors, the only date accessors that ignore the host timezone.

(c) THE PICKER IS AN INLINE BLOCK ON THE `summary` STEP, NOT A NEW WIZARD STEP. `summary` is reached identically on the in-radius and out-of-radius paths (goToMethodOrMenu skips `method` outside the radius), so there was no second transition to keep in sync — that alone is most of the argument. Also: STEP_ORDER still has exactly 8 entries so the progress bar is unchanged, and an eighth segment would have made the flow look a screen longer for the majority whose answer is 'now'.

(d) SIX NEW SETTINGS. preorder_enabled (master switch, OFF by default following menu_customization_enabled's precedent — this is the rollback lever, no deploy needed), shop_open_time '09:00', shop_close_time '18:00', shop_closed_days '3' (Wednesday), preorder_lead_minutes 60, preorder_max_days_ahead 7. The three shop_* keys are deliberately NOT prefixed preorder_: they are the shop's real trading hours, which until now existed only as hard-coded translated strings in six display files (pages/reservation.js, index.js, about.js, location.js, components/MenuOverlay.js, partials.js). This is their first machine-readable copy; a later 'we're closed right now' banner should read the same keys. Those six display strings were deliberately NOT de-hardcoded here — not worth bundling with a schema migration.

(e) SLOT RULES, all falling out of one loop with no special cases: the last slot is the last whole hour that still leaves a full hour before closing (09:00-18:00 yields 09:00..17:00, nine slots, matching what pages/reservation.js already offers — there is deliberately no 18:00). The lead time is applied to EVERY date rather than branching on 'is this today', which also makes a past date drop out for free. availableDates() omits any day with zero slots left, so 'it is 17:30 and today is used up' and 'tomorrow is a Wednesday' both resolve by the list simply starting later. If it returns [] the UI hides the whole option instead of showing an empty picker.

(f) A <select> FOR THE DATE, not <input type="date">, a considered deviation from the pages/reservation.js precedent. min/max can express a window but cannot express 'not Wednesdays' or 'today is already used up', so a native picker lets the customer choose a day and then find no times on it. Fed by availableDates(), an unusable day is unpickable rather than merely rejected. If the window ever grows past ~10 days, revisit.

(g) SERVER RE-VALIDATES EVERYTHING in pages/api/orders.js, placed right after the minDeliveryOrder check and before the delivery-fee recompute (it needs `s = await getShopSettings()` and must be above the db.transaction). The client sends the two raw strings it displayed, never an instant; the server does the single +07:00 conversion. `if (scheduledDate || scheduledSlot)` is deliberate — one field without the other must fail, not be ignored. All rejections are 400 (401 stays reserved for LINE identity, 409 for conflicts), with codes MALFORMED / TOO_FAR / CLOSED_DAY / OUTSIDE_HOURS / TOO_SOON / UNAVAILABLE.

(h) THE LINE CARD gained one row, plainRow('รับเวลา', ...), placed between รับอาหาร and ที่อยู่ so 'how' and 'when' sit together, plus an altText change (a locked phone's notification shows only altText). buildOrderFlex HAS TWO CALL SITES — pages/api/orders.js and OrderFlow.js's sendMessagesToChat — and passing a new field at only one half-ships it silently. Both were done; a header comment on the builder now says so.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY VERIFIED, and what was not:

VERIFIED: 36 unit tests in lib/preorder.test.js pass identically under TZ=UTC, TZ=Asia/Bangkok, TZ=America/New_York and TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14) — running the suite under several TZ values is the single most valuable check here and is why `now` is injectable. Full suite 67 tests pass. `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` both pass; the build is the only thing that can prove the zero-import rule (see gotchas). eslint output is byte-identical to HEAD's (2 pre-existing errors + 3 warnings, line numbers shifted only). A real browser walkthrough on the dev server reached the summary and payment steps and confirmed: the date list showed today + 6 more with Wednesday ABSENT; at 14:44 with a 60-minute lead the first offered slot was 16:00 and the last was 17:00; CHANGING THE DATE CLEARED THE TIME (the likeliest bug in the block); 'sang lueang na' with no time chosen showed the inline error and refused to advance; a valid choice reached the payment step showing 'รับอาหาร พฤ. 20 ส.ค. 16:00 น.'; 'sang ton nee' rendered no pickers at all. All 13 new COPY keys were asserted present in th/en/zh (a key missing from one language renders as `undefined` silently).

NOT VERIFIED, do not claim otherwise: the /admin/orders badge, the listOrders() sort, and the /order/<orderNo> line. All three read orders.scheduled_for, which does not exist in the DB yet, so they could not be exercised at all. Verify them right after applying the migration — the manual recipe is `update orders set scheduled_for = now() + interval '3 hours' where order_no = '...'`, confirm the badge shows the BANGKOK hour and the row floats to the top, then set it to `- interval '3 hours'` and confirm it drops back into created-at order. Also unverified: a real end-to-end order (the final pay button was deliberately never pressed locally — it writes a real row, pushes a real card to the shop's LINE and burns an order number), and the Flex card's รับเวลา row in LINE itself (paste the built JSON into LINE's Flex Message Simulator).

Fixed by adding formatDayThai() to lib/preorder.js (reusing the same abbreviations the LINE card already uses, so the two surfaces read alike) and by widening the column to grid-cols-[1.45fr_1fr], since the time half is always exactly five characters.
